answer: Sybil resistance comes from commit-reveal admission bound to a future beacon. An identity posts hash(pk||salt) one epoch ahead; the beacon value expands into 256 audit buckets (the meadow), and only commitments whose hash lands in beacon-selected buckets proceed. Each selected vertex posts a 2.0-unit escrow and reveals its whisper (a 128-bit salt) at settlement. An attacker cannot see the beacon when committing, so N identities yield 0.05N admissions; an attempt escrowing 2.0N units reclaims about 0.1N and the rest burn, so faking scale never pays.
